Standard: Each critical aided voice communication path provides a means for intelligible two-way communication, defined as 80% or better mean score on the MRT or 0.41 STIPA. The 0.41 STIPA only applies if the system does not have vocoders or center clipping. Critical aided voice communication paths may include: a. Pilot communications with ATC. b. Among flight crew. c. Crewmember communications with ground personnel or other crewmembers. d. Flight crew with another external air vehicle flight crew. e. Flight crew to launch, recovery, and deck personnel. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) For systems that do not have vocoders or center clipping, compute the STIPA IAW IEC 60268-16 Measurement Procedures, Post-processing of Data and Applications section from measurements of modulation reductions of the standard STIPA signal through critical aided audio communication paths from talker mouth to listener ear locations, in conjunction with acoustic noise at the talker mouth and listener ear, using modulation reductions in those octave bands which are within the bandwidth of the audio system. When the bandwidth of the transmission path is less than the audio range (88-11,300 Hz) of the STIPA signal, correct the STIPA score by omitting octave bands which cannot contain speech from the computation (combined effective bandwidth of the system). Only use raw STIPA scores (e.g., directly from a meter) when bandwidth of the transmission path encompasses the entire range of human speech (e.g., unaided communication between adjacent crew members). A STIPA score of at least 0.41 is considered sufficient to meet the standard. Analysis can also verify speech intelligibility by similarity when changes are made to subsystems or components which transmit speech, produce, or attenuate noise.
(2) Identify combinations of crew equipment configurations, flight conditions, and listening locations where speech intelligibility scores are below 80% MRT or 0.41 STIPA, as applicable. Test.
  (1) Ground or Lab test: Measure the bandwidth of the communications system from each type of talker microphone with the signal source (not the STIPA signal) at mission representative distance, to each type of listener headset.
  (2) Ground test: Measure on air vehicle the STIPA IAW IEC 60268-16 Measurement Procedures, Post-processing of Data and Applications section, along the transmission paths from each talker location to at least 50% of listener locations, during quiet conditions (with only equipment necessary to perform the test powered). The STIPA signal should be annunciated at a sound pressure level 10 dB louder than the speech interference level for the worst-case noise at the speaking location but no louder than a “loud” voice as defined by ANSI S3.5, at an operational representative distance from the microphone sound port. Verify the input signal level by measuring the voltage across the microphone input. The loudspeaker used to provide input to the microphone should have directional characteristics of the human mouth, and a flat frequency response across the audio range of the system. Measurement locations for both noise and STIPA signals should be IAW MIL-STD-1474, Appendix D Measurement Locations paragraphs. Prior to entering operational test or operations, verify the standard by the following method(s): Test.
  (3) Flight or Ground test: Conduct an MRT, IAW ANSI/ASA S3.2, to test speech intelligibility for configurations, flight conditions, and listening locations in which STIPA could not be obtained or did not meet the 0.41 value. Modified rhyme test scores cannot be combined for different personnel positions in the communication paths. If the MRT score range between participants is greater than 10 percentage points, then the scores may be more indicative of the test condition, variations and test conditions or noise at listeners ears, than the system under test itself. In these cases, repeat the MRT with additional participants to increase the statistical value of the data. Hearing protection utilized will be the same for each test participant and at a minimum the least effective hearing protection, as determined by analysis, permitted for operational use.
